query: What different aspects of their purchase are Amazon reviewers actually talking about?

per_column.name: primary_aspect
per_column.rationale: Directly answers the query by giving an aspect axis to group reviews on -- highly useful. However, groundedness is shaky: the categories skew toward physical-product aspects (quality/performance/design/comfort/packaging) that don't fit media/book/music reviews. Row AMZ-0001 (availability of a black doll, not product quality) and AMZ-0003 (an artist's emotional depth) are both labelled 'quality' as a catch-all, and AMZ-0002 (book content critique) also collapses to 'quality'. These are loose, not clearly warranted readings of the specific source text.

per_column.name: has_complaint
per_column.rationale: A complaint flag gives a useful cross-cutting axis for the query, though it edges toward a generic sentiment flag. Groundedness is undermined by clear errors: AMZ-0003 is an entirely hostile put-down of the artist yet is marked 'no', and AMZ-0001 is a frustrated complaint about unavailability marked 'yes' correctly, but the inconsistency shows the values are not reliably read from text.

per_column.name: comparison_mentions
per_column.rationale: Counting explicit comparisons to other products/works is a genuine new analytical axis relevant to what reviewers discuss. Values look well-grounded in the samples: AMZ-0005 references 'The Departed' and hot contemporary releases (=1), and rows without comparisons get 0. AMZ-0004 mentions 'the only one out there' which arguably implies a comparison but scoring 0 is defensible.

judge.rationale: All three columns provide legitimate, non-redundant axes (aspect, complaint presence, comparison count) that genuinely help answer what reviewers are talking about, so analytical usefulness is strong. Groundedness is the weaker dimension: primary_aspect uses a physical-product taxonomy that misfits many media/book reviews and collapses distinct concerns into 'quality', and has_complaint shows at least one contradiction with the source text (AMZ-0003). comparison_mentions is the best-grounded of the three.
